content.s: Apple's current Mac guide documents five ways to tile windows: drag to an edge, hold Option while dragging, use the green button, choose layouts from the Window menu, or use keyboard shortcuts. Common halves, quarters, centering, filling, and multi-window arrangements no longer require a separate utility.

items.s: Open System Settings, choose Desktop & Dock, then review the Windows tiling options.
Drag to an edge or corner.
Release when the destination area highlights.
Hold Option while dragging toward a highlighted area.
Use the green button for layouts.
Hover over it to choose Move & Resize or Fill & Arrange options.

content.s: Rectangle's official site describes a free open-source Mac app that moves and resizes windows with keyboard shortcuts or snap areas. It supports Intel and Apple silicon and remains the sensible first third-party choice when built-in tiling is not fast or configurable enough. Read

blocks.text: Moom and Magnet: layouts or simplicity

content.s: Moom belongs on the shortlist when you want saved arrangements and custom layouts that restore a working setup. Magnet fits people who want familiar halves, thirds, quarters, and shortcuts without building an automation system. Verify current compatibility and pricing on each official page before buying.

BetterTouchTool makes sense when window placement is one action in a larger custom trigger system. It can connect gestures, keyboard input, app-specific conditions, and window actions. That power is useful when you enjoy configuration; it is unnecessary for a person who only wants left and right halves.

blocks.text: Gojo: window snapping as part of a Mac superapp

content.s: Gojo lets you preview, focus, organize, and snap windows from the MacBook notch. It is deliberately less specialized than Rectangle or Moom. blocks.text: Why third-party window tools need Accessibility access

content.s: A third-party window manager must interact with windows owned by other apps. On macOS, that commonly requires Accessibility permission to inspect, focus, move, or resize those windows. Grant it only to software you trust, and remove access in System Settings when you stop using the app.

Some windows cannot be moved or resized normally because the app fixes their dimensions, uses a nonstandard window, or restricts system accessibility actions. A failed snap is not always a window manager bug.
